identification.summary: Silk Typhoon (formerly HAFNIUM) is a Chinese espionage group. Microsoft describes it as well-resourced and technically efficient, able to quickly operationalize exploits for zero-day vulnerabilities in edge devices, and holding one of the largest targeting footprints among Chinese threat actors [S1]. It is best known for exploiting four on-premises Exchange Server zero-days in early 2021 [S1][S2]. Since late 2024 Microsoft has observed it shift toward IT supply-chain compromise: it steals API keys and credentials from privileged access management (PAM), remote monitoring and management, cloud application and cloud data management providers, then uses them to reach those providers' downstream customers [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft says it has tracked the actor since 2020 and observed Exchange zero-day exploitation beginning in January 2021 [S1]. The US indictment of two alleged HAFNIUM operators covers intrusions from February 2020 to June 2021, as reported by the press [S3].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Silk Typhoon (formerly HAFNIUM) [S1]. CrowdStrike tracks MURKY PANDA, active since at least 2023, and says that cluster's activity aligns with what industry tracks as Silk Typhoon. This is an overlap statement, not an identity [S5][S6]. MITRE tracks the group as HAFNIUM (G0125) [S10]. Some press coverage of the March 2025 APT27 / i-Soon indictments labels Yin Kecheng and Zhou Shuai 'Silk Typhoon', while other coverage of the same indictments uses APT27 and lists aliases such as Emissary Panda and Lucky Mouse. Those aliases sit under Linen Typhoon in this encyclopedia; see gaps [S9].

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China, Ministry of State Security (MSS). A US indictment unsealed in July 2025 alleges that Xu Zewei and Zhang Yu acted at the direction of the MSS Shanghai State Security Bureau. Xu allegedly worked through Shanghai Powerock Network Co. Ltd., which prosecutors called an 'enabling' company (as reported by the press) [S3][S4].
attribution.confidence: In 2021 Microsoft attributed the Exchange campaign to HAFNIUM with high confidence, as a group assessed to be state-sponsored and operating out of China [S2]. In 2025 Microsoft called Silk Typhoon a Chinese state actor but stated no confidence level [S1]. The US government has charged alleged HAFNIUM operators criminally, which is an indictment, not a conviction [S3][S4]. Linking the 2024 Treasury breach to Silk Typhoon rests on Bloomberg reporting citing people familiar with the incident [S7].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and incident analysis [S1][S2]; a DOJ indictment and the extradition of Xu Zewei from Italy, known here through press coverage [S3][S4]; and CrowdStrike reporting on the overlapping MURKY PANDA cluster [S5][S6].

objectives: Espionage. Microsoft says the data it seeks overlaps with China-based interests, US government policy and administration, and legal process and documents tied to law enforcement investigations [S1]. In 2020 the group allegedly sought COVID-19 vaccine, treatment and testing research from US universities, including one in Texas (as reported from the indictment) [S3][S4]. In the 2024 Treasury intrusion the group reportedly accessed unclassified information on potential sanctions actions [S7].

sectors: IT services and infrastructure, including MSPs and RMM providers [S1]
PAM, identity management, cloud application and cloud data management providers [S1][S5]
Government, including US federal (Treasury) and state and local [S1][S7]
Healthcare and infectious-disease or COVID-19 researchers [S1][S2][S3]
regions: Worldwide; Microsoft says targets are in the US and worldwide [S1]
targeting.notes: Microsoft says downstream victims of the late-2024 supply-chain activity were mostly state and local government and the IT sector [S1]. The FBI said the 2021 Exchange campaign victimized more than 12,700 US organizations (as reported in press coverage of the DOJ case) [S4].

capabilities.summary: Edge-device and server exploitation: Exchange CVE-2021-26855, -26857, -26858 and -27065 (2021); Citrix NetScaler CVE-2023-3519 and zero-days (early 2024); Palo Alto GlobalProtect CVE-2024-3400 (March 2024); and an Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day, CVE-2025-0282 (January 2025) [S1][S2]. CrowdStrike says MURKY PANDA also used zero-days against SaaS providers, and coverage of its report includes a Commvault product zero-day [S5][S6]. Credential access includes password spraying and corporate passwords leaked on public repositories such as GitHub [S1]. Post-exploitation includes web shells, Active Directory dumping, theft of key-vault secrets, and LSASS dumping with Procdump [S1][S2]. In 2021 the group used Covenant C2, Nishang and PowerCat, staged data with 7-Zip and exfiltrated to MEGA [S2]. The group moves from on-premises to cloud through AADConnect/Entra Connect servers. It abuses service principals and OAuth apps (including by adding credentials to already-consented apps) to pull mail, OneDrive and SharePoint data through Microsoft Graph and EWS, and it creates Entra ID apps disguised as legitimate services [S1]. It has abused delegated administrative privileges held by a Microsoft cloud solution provider [S5][S6]. For anti-forensics it clears logs and modifies timestamps [S1][S5]. Its toolset includes the Neo-reGeorg web shell and a Golang Linux RAT that CrowdStrike calls CloudedHope [S5][S6].

campaigns.name: COVID-19 research intrusions
campaigns.summary: The alleged operators Xu Zewei and Zhang Yu targeted US universities and immunology and virology researchers, including a Texas university, to obtain COVID-19 research, reportedly under MSS Shanghai State Security Bureau direction (as reported from the indictment).

campaigns.name: Exchange Server zero-day campaign (ProxyLogon chain)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft attributes exploitation of four on-premises Exchange zero-days, followed by web shells, LSASS dumping and mailbox exfiltration, to HAFNIUM. The FBI later said more than 12,700 US entities were victimized.

campaigns.name: Citrix NetScaler and GlobalProtect exploitation
campaigns.summary: Microsoft observed exploitation of NetScaler zero-days and of CVE-2023-3519, and in March 2024 zero-day exploitation of Palo Alto GlobalProtect CVE-2024-3400.

campaigns.name: US Treasury breach via BeyondTrust API key
campaigns.summary: A stolen BeyondTrust Remote Support SaaS API key gave access to Treasury workstations, including OFAC. Bloomberg attributed the breach to Silk Typhoon, citing people familiar with the incident. In January 2025 Treasury sanctioned Yin Kecheng over the Departmental Offices compromise; Treasury did not name Silk Typhoon in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: IT supply-chain compromise
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says the group used API keys and credentials stolen from PAM, cloud application and data-management providers to access downstream tenants, mostly state and local government and IT-sector victims.

campaigns.name: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day (CVE-2025-0282)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft observed zero-day exploitation by Silk Typhoon and reported the flaw to Ivanti, which fixed it.

campaigns.name: APT27 / i-Soon indictments (naming conflict)
campaigns.summary: DOJ charged alleged APT27 hackers Yin Kecheng and Zhou Shuai. Some press labeled them 'Silk Typhoon', but this encyclopedia does not adopt that mapping.

campaigns.name: Arrest of Xu Zewei in Milan
campaigns.summary: Italian authorities arrested Xu on 3 July 2025 at US request, and a nine-count US indictment against Xu and Zhang Yu was unsealed. Zhang remains at large.

campaigns.name: MURKY PANDA trusted-relationship cloud compromises
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike reported that the cluster used SaaS-provider zero-days and Entra ID secrets to read downstream customer email, and abused a Microsoft cloud solution provider's delegated admin privileges.

campaigns.name: Extradition of Xu Zewei
campaigns.summary: Xu was extradited from Italy and appeared in US District Court in Houston, Texas.

diamond.adversary: MSS-directed operators, including contractors. Xu Zewei of Shanghai Powerock Network Co. and Zhang Yu were allegedly tasked by the Shanghai State Security Bureau [S3][S4]. Microsoft calls the group a Chinese state actor [S1].
diamond.capability: Rapid zero-day and n-day exploitation of edge devices and servers (Exchange, NetScaler, GlobalProtect, Ivanti), web shells, credential and secret theft, and Entra ID / OAuth / service-principal abuse for cloud data theft [S1][S2]. The overlapping MURKY PANDA cluster adds Neo-reGeorg and CloudedHope [S5][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: No dedicated infrastructure. The group relies on covert networks of compromised Cyberoam appliances, Zyxel routers and QNAP devices, plus proxies, VPNs and short-lease VPS [S1]. In 2021 it operated mainly from leased US VPS and exfiltrated to MEGA [S2].
diamond.victim: US government at federal, state and local levels; IT service providers and SaaS vendors as stepping stones; and defense, healthcare and research, legal, higher education, think tanks, NGOs and energy [S1][S2][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Intelligence on US government policy and administration, legal and law-enforcement matters, sanctions deliberations and pandemic research, reflecting PRC state interests [S1][S3][S7].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing appliances and on-premises servers, hybrid identity (Entra Connect), multi-tenant and OAuth apps, and trust relationships between providers and customers (API keys, delegated admin privileges) [S1][S5].

gaps: No primary DOJ, Treasury or FBI documents could be opened (blocked); indictment and sanctions details come from press coverage [S3][S4][S7][S8].
The CrowdStrike MURKY PANDA blog post could not be fetched; details come from secondary coverage. CrowdStrike frames MURKY PANDA as aligning with Silk Typhoon, not as identical to it [S5][S6].
The Silk Typhoon attribution of the Treasury breach rests on Bloomberg's anonymous sourcing; the government sources gathered name Yin Kecheng, not Silk Typhoon [S7][S8].

Naming conflict: some press labels the March 2025 APT27 indictees (Yin Kecheng, Zhou Shuai) 'Silk Typhoon', while those aliases (APT27, Emissary Panda, Lucky Mouse) map to Linen Typhoon in this encyclopedia. The primary indictment text was not reviewed [S9].

Some press links Silk Typhoon or HAFNIUM to Mandiant's UNC5221, the cluster Google associated with Ivanti exploitation. This was not confirmed in a vendor primary source, so UNC5221 is not added as an alias.
Imported aliases ATK233, Operation Exchange Marauder, Red Dev 13 and 'timmy' were not verified in sources gathered.
The full extent of downstream victims of the 2024-2025 supply-chain activity and of the Commvault-related intrusions is not public in the sources gathered.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain includes internet-facing VPN and edge appliances (Ivanti, NetScaler, GlobalProtect), hybrid identity servers (Entra Connect), and third-party IT, PAM, RMM and SaaS providers that hold API keys or delegated admin rights into DoD and DIB tenants [S1][S5]. STEP 2: The group can turn new edge-device CVEs into exploits within days. Its use of covert networks of compromised SOHO devices and short-lease VPS undermines IP-reputation blocking [S1]. STEP 3: The template is edge-device or provider compromise, then web shell, credential and key-vault theft, then a pivot to Entra ID through service principals or OAuth apps, then mail and SharePoint/OneDrive exfiltration via Graph or EWS, with log clearing [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is persistent collection of policy, legal and sanctions-related email and documents from government and contractor tenants through compromised providers [S1][S7]. MDCOA is mass zero-day exploitation of a widely deployed edge product across DoD-adjacent networks during a crisis, as in the Exchange 2021 campaign with more than 12,700 US victims, to harvest planning data at scale [S2][S4]. Candidate indicators: new or renamed Entra ID apps with Office 365-themed names; new credentials added to consented apps; Graph or EWS mail access by service principals; unexpected web shells on edge devices or servers; admin-account resets through provider APIs; and logons from SOHO-device IP space [S1][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: fuse edge-appliance patch status and third-party provider access (API keys, delegated admin privileges) into the common operating picture, because the actor enters through these trust paths [S1][S5]. (2) Authorities: the activity crosses DoD, DIB, commercial SaaS and federal civilian networks (Treasury), so response requires coordinating DC3, CISA and FBI lanes rather than unilateral DoD action [S1][S7]. (3) Mission assurance: inventory and minimize standing provider privileges and multi-tenant app consents, and plan for credential and key rotation at the provider level after a compromise [S1]. (4) Coordination: law-enforcement actions (the Xu Zewei arrest and extradition) have not been assessed as stopping operations, so keep defensive posture independent of indictment news [S3][S4].

provenance.importedSummary: HAFNIUM primarily targets entities in the United States across a number of industry sectors, including infectious disease researchers, law firms, higher education institutions, defense contractors, policy think tanks, and NGOs. Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center (MSTIC) attributes this campaign with high confidence to HAFNIUM, a group assessed to be state-sponsored and operating out of China, based on observed victimology, tactics and procedures. HAFNIUM has previously compromised victims by exploiting vulnerabilities in internet-facing servers, and has used legitimate open-source frameworks, like Covenant, for command and control. Once they’ve gained access to a victim network, HAFNIUM typically exfiltrates data to file sharing sites like MEGA.In campaigns unrelated to these vulnerabilities, Microsoft has observed HAFNIUM interacting with victim Office 365 tenants. While they are often unsuccessful in compromising customer accounts, this reconnaissance activity helps the adversary identify more details about their targets’ environments. HAFNIUM operates primarily from leased virtual private servers (VPS) in the United States.
